title: Huevos rancheros
description: Fried eggs on warm tortillas with crushed black beans, warm salsa, cheese and avocado. A big Mexican farm breakfast.
steps: Drain and rinse the beans and warm them in a small pan with a spoon of water, crushing some with a fork. Warm the salsa in another small pan.
Warm the tortillas in a dry frying pan for a few seconds on each side and put them on plates.

steps.text: Heat the oil in the frying pan on medium and fry the eggs for 3 to 4 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks still runny.
steps.tip: Put a lid on for the last moment if the tops of the whites stay clear.

steps: Spread the beans on the tortillas, put the eggs on top and spoon the warm salsa around them.

steps.text: Finish with grated cheese, sliced avocado and a pinch of chili.
steps.tip: Ranchero means ranch style: a farm breakfast to keep you going till lunch.

title: Apple and cinnamon baked oats
description: Oats, apple, raisins and walnuts baked with milk and egg into a soft, sliceable breakfast. Make it once, eat it for days.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C and butter a baking dish of about 20 x 25 cm.
Core and dice two of the apples and slice the third thinly for the top. Chop the walnuts.
In a bowl mix the oats, baking powder, cinnamon, raisins, walnuts and diced apple.
Whisk the milk, eggs and honey, pour it over the oats, stir and tip everything into the dish.

steps.text: Lay the apple slices on top and bake for 35 minutes until set and golden.
steps.tip: It should be firm in the middle, like a soft cake.

steps.text: Cut into squares. Eat it warm, or cold from the fridge with yogurt.
steps.tip: It keeps 4 days. Warm a square in the microwave for a quick breakfast.

title: Spinach and feta egg muffins
description: Little baked omelettes with spinach, pepper and feta. A protein-rich breakfast or snack you can grab from the fridge.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180 °C. Oil a 12-hole muffin tin well, or use silicone or paper cases.
steps.tip: Egg sticks badly to metal, so oil every hole.

steps: Chop the spinach, pepper and spring onion small. Divide them and the crumbled feta between the holes.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with the milk and pepper and pour over the vegetables, filling each hole about three quarters full.
steps.tip: No salt needed: the feta brings enough.

steps: Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until puffed and just set in the middle.

steps.text: Let them cool for 5 minutes, then loosen them with a knife and lift them out. Two make a portion.
steps.tip: They sink a little as they cool. They keep 4 days; warm them for a few seconds in the microwave.

title: Pear and ricotta toast with honey
description: Toast spread thickly with ricotta, topped with sliced pear, walnuts, honey and cinnamon. Five minutes, no cooking skills needed.
steps: Toast the bread until golden.

steps.text: Core the pear and slice it thinly. Chop the walnuts.
steps.tip: A ripe pear that smells sweet near the stem works best.

steps: Spread the ricotta thickly on the toast and fan the pear slices over it.
Drizzle with the honey and scatter with the walnuts and a pinch of cinnamon.

title: Puff pastry cheese straws
description: Twisted strips of puff pastry with cheese, paprika and sesame, baked until crisp. A savoury snack that keeps all week.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C and line a baking tray with baking paper. Grate the cheese finely and beat the egg.
Unroll the pastry. Brush it with egg and sprinkle half the cheese and the paprika over one half.
Fold the other half over, press it down with a rolling pin, brush the top with egg and sprinkle with the rest of the cheese and the sesame seeds.

steps.text: Cut into strips about 1.5 cm wide. Twist each strip a few times and lay it on the tray, pressing the ends down.
steps.tip: Pressing the ends down stops them untwisting in the oven.

steps: Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until puffed and golden.

steps.text: Let them cool on the tray, then keep them in a tin.
steps.tip: They keep 5 days. Crisp them in the oven for a few minutes if they soften.

title: Honey and cinnamon roasted nuts
description: Almonds, cashews and walnuts roasted with honey and cinnamon until crunchy. A small handful is a filling snack.
steps: Heat the oven to 170 °C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Warm the honey for a few seconds until runny and mix it with the cinnamon and salt.
Toss the nuts in the honey until coated and spread them in one layer on the tray.

steps.text: Roast for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring once, until golden and fragrant.
steps.tip: Watch them at the end: honey goes from golden to burnt quickly.

steps.text: Let them cool completely on the tray, then break up any clumps and keep them in a jar.
steps.tip: They are sticky when hot and turn crunchy as they cool. A small handful, about 30 g, is a portion.

title: Pumpkin spice muffins
description: Soft muffins with grated pumpkin, cinnamon and ginger, topped with pumpkin seeds. An autumn snack that also works for breakfast.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases.

steps.text: Peel the pumpkin and grate it finely.
steps.tip: Hokkaido or butternut pumpkin is sweetest. Squeeze it lightly if it is very wet.

steps: Whisk the eggs, sugar, oil and yogurt in a large bowl and stir in the pumpkin.

steps.text: Mix the flour, baking powder, cinnamon, ginger and nutmeg and fold them into the wet mix until just combined.
steps.tip: Stop as soon as there is no dry flour. A lumpy batter makes light muffins.

steps.text: Fill the cases, sprinkle with the pumpkin seeds and bake for 20 to 22 minutes until risen and golden.
steps.tip: A skewer pushed into the middle should come out clean.

steps.text: Cool them in the tin for 5 minutes, then on a rack.
steps.tip: They keep 4 days in a closed box and freeze well.

title: Lemon drizzle cake
description: A buttery loaf cake soaked while still hot with lemon syrup, which sets into a crisp, sugary crust.

steps.text: Take the butter out of the fridge early so it is soft. Heat the oven to 180 °C and line a loaf tin with baking paper.
steps.tip: Soft butter dents easily when you press it.

steps.text: Beat the butter and sugar for 3 minutes until pale and fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time.
steps.tip: If it looks curdled, add a spoon of the flour and keep beating.

steps: Grate in the zest of both lemons. Fold in the flour mixed with the baking powder, and the milk.

steps.text: Spoon into the tin, smooth the top and bake for 40 to 45 minutes.
steps.tip: A skewer pushed into the middle should come out clean.

steps: While it bakes, mix the juice of both lemons with the powdered sugar.

steps.text: As soon as the cake comes out, prick it all over with a skewer and spoon the lemon syrup over it slowly. Let it cool in the tin.
steps.tip: The hot cake drinks up the syrup and the top sets into a crisp crust. It keeps 5 days.

title: Pear and almond cake
description: A moist cake made with ground almonds, with pear slices pressed into the top. Lovely with coffee.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line a round cake tin of about 22 cm. Grind the almonds finely in a blender.
steps.tip: Stop before they turn into a paste.

steps: Beat the soft butter, sugar and vanilla sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Fold in the ground almonds, flour and baking powder.
Spread the batter in the tin. Peel, core and slice the pears and press the slices into the top in a ring.

steps.text: Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
steps.tip: If the top browns too fast, cover it loosely with foil.

steps.text: Let it cool in the tin, then dust with the powdered sugar.
steps.tip: The almonds keep it moist for 4 days.

title: One-bowl chocolate cake
description: A dark, moist chocolate tray cake mixed in a single bowl and covered in a simple chocolate glaze.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line a tin of about 20 x 30 cm with baking paper.
Put the flour, sugar, cocoa, baking powder, baking soda and vanilla sugar in a large bowl and mix.

steps.text: Add the eggs, milk, oil and {100 ml} hot water and whisk until smooth. The batter is runny, which is right.
steps.tip: Hot water makes the cocoa taste richer and the cake extra moist.

steps.text: Pour into the tin and bake for 30 to 35 minutes.
steps.tip: A skewer pushed into the middle should come out clean.

steps: Let the cake cool. Heat the cream until steaming, pour it over the chopped chocolate and stir until smooth.

steps.text: Spread the glaze over the cake and let it set before cutting.
steps.tip: It keeps 5 days under a cover.

title: Revani (Greek semolina orange cake)
description: A light semolina and yogurt cake soaked in orange syrup and cut into diamonds. Sweet, sticky and better the next day.

steps.text: Grate the zest of the oranges and keep it. Squeeze their juice into a pot with {200 g} of the sugar and {250 ml} water, bring to the boil, simmer for 5 minutes and let it cool.
steps.tip: Cold syrup on a hot cake is the rule: it soaks in without making the cake soggy.

steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line a tin of about 20 x 30 cm with baking paper.
Whisk the eggs and the rest of the sugar for 5 minutes until pale and thick. Whisk in the yogurt, oil and orange zest.
Fold in the semolina, flour and baking powder. Pour into the tin and bake for 35 to 40 minutes until golden.
As soon as it comes out, cut it into diamonds and pour the cold syrup slowly over the hot cake.

steps.text: Leave it to soak for at least an hour before serving.
steps.tip: It gets better the next day and keeps 5 days, covered.
